svg.text: ux.md · vision.md · design.md ARE ALL INTERPRETATIONS OF RESEARCH
A pile of findings does not contain user needs. Findings record what happened. A need, a concept, a behaviour — each is a claim about what should be true for one product.
Somebody authors each of those. That authoring is where the product value is created, it is legitimately not evidence, and it has to be marked as what it is.
Blue = research owns · red = UX owns · amber = the authoring step · green = the loop that refills the evidence.
findings.yaml
WHAT HAPPENED. Someone did a thing, or said a thing.
Holds SECONDARY and PRIMARY both.
population_fidelity says which: primary · proxy · internal · none
claim_scope says how far: existence · pattern · prevalence
Research authors AND grades. Nothing downstream may overwrite.
NOT TAILORED TO ANY PRODUCT
A finding is true about the people it came from, on the date it was
gathered, against the build it was gathered on. It is not about your
feature — it cannot be, and asking it to be is how scope gets widened.
A secondary finding is still a finding. `population_fidelity: none`
caps it at LOW; it does not make it absent.
THE AUTHORING STEP — abduction. Owned by UX. Not a finding, not an unsupported guess. A third thing.
Her vocabulary already has every slot: claim_type: inferred · status: hypothesis · origin: design · invalidates_if · G17 caps it until research backs it.
Nothing REQUIRES them where the authoring happens. That is the hole in both halves: hers stops overclaiming, mine stops dropping, neither marks the leap.
ux.md — authors THE NEED
"Given this evidence, here is the problem, and whose it is."
scope: existence / pattern — claims about what IS
rung: inferred, resting on observed + stated findings
✓ ## Evidence · ceiling check runs
THE NEED IS NEW CONTENT, NOT A RESTATEMENT
This is where a need statement first exists. It is not in findings.yaml
and could not be — findings are about what happened, needs about what
should be true. Authored, and still ungradeable above what it rests on.
Limitation: rests_on: takes ONE finding. A need usually rests on several.
vision.md — authors THE CONCEPTS
"Given this evidence, here is what would be valuable."
Concepts, blueprints, multiple futures side by side.
Interprets findings too — often SECONDARY ones.
scope: existence / pattern. NEVER prevalence.
Runs honestly at LOW. That is not a defect — it is what a
vision is. The defect is LOW travelling downstream unmarked.
WHERE HER RULES AND YOUR METHOD ACTUALLY COLLIDE
Her prohibition: "no confidence by volume — three Low findings pointing the
same way are three Low findings, not one Medium." Correct.
Your method: a secondary dive first, because independent convergence tells
you the shape of the space. Also correct.
Resolved by claim_scope: convergence supports EXISTENCE and PATTERN.
It never supports PREVALENCE. Volume widens scope, not confidence.
design.md — authors THE BEHAVIOUR
"Given this evidence, here is how it must behave."
scope: usability — can they do it, did they do it unaided
the one file with claims resting on STANDARDS, not findings:
WCAG, APEX, the FLOOR items. Those need no evidence row.
SECONDARY EVIDENCE STOPS BEING ENOUGH HERE
Convergent desk research can tell you the conversation is the human half.
It cannot tell you whether your approval step is reachable by keyboard.
This is the row where population_fidelity has to be primary.
FLOOR items are the only claims in the system legitimately unsourced.
Intent Spec §5 → the build
THE COMMITMENT. UXI-## · append-only · inherits forward.
Where code spec-driven design starts. Everything above is the
part code SDD assumes someone else already got right.
A ROW CAN OUTLIVE ITS BASIS
The id survives a re-grade; the justification quietly does not. Nothing
re-opens a UXI row when research lowers the finding under it — the
missing half of "it is a loop, not a snapshot."
AND THE STACK IS NOT A ONE-WAY TRIP — how the work actually runs
1 · SECONDARY DIVE
are there already
obvious good answers?
fidelity: none → LOW
2 · INTERPRET
author the need and
the concepts on what
secondary will carry
3 · PLAN
what would falsify
this? invalidates_if
IS the research plan
4 · PRIMARY
go and get the thing
secondary could not
answer · fidelity: primary
5 · RE-INTERPRET
the finding is regraded, so
every interpretation resting
on it is now claiming too much
↑ and round again
